notes: SDSS J140306.54+145005.0 is included as the third Possible HVS listed in Table 1 (I:p6-b0). The text at T:p7-b3 instead gives SDSS J141342.50+442550.03, but the appendix table (I:p9-b0) classifies SDSS J141342.51+442550.0 as a QSO; I treat that text entry as a printing/coordinate error and do not list the QSO as a star. HVS2 (US 708): the Table 1 entry 'US 7082' (I:p6-b0) carries a trailing reference footnote, not a digit of the name. HVS3 (HE 0437-5439): the Table 1 entry 'HE 0437-54393' (I:p6-b0) likewise has a trailing reference footnote, and T:p1-b12 supports HE 0437-5439. HVS15 was previously called a possibly bound HVS (T:p6-b4), but this paper's final assessment is very likely unbound (T:p6-b5), so it is recorded under candidates_found. HD 271791 is included as a follow_up unbound hyper-runaway, not as one of the survey HVSs. The four Possible HVSs are retained as candidates_found only under the Xue et al. escape-velocity model (T:p7-b2; T:p7-b4). Stars under Table 1's 'Possible Bound HVSs' heading (I:p6-b0) are not listed because the paper does not retain them as Galactic unbound candidates and provides no explicit prior unbound identification.

HVS1: HVS1 is identified as the first HVS and as SDSS J090744.99+024506.91. Table 1 reports R_GC = 111 kpc, heliocentric radial velocity 840 km/s, and v_rf = 696 km/s; the paper explicitly states that v_rf is a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity (T:p7-b6). The introduction reports the discovery-paper value of at least +700 ± 12 km/s at a distance of 110 kpc (T:p1-b6). The 110 kpc is treated as Galactocentric because it is consistent with the Table 1 R_GC value. No explicit RA/Dec columns or parallax/proper-motion measurements for HVS1 are given in the supplied material; the catalog designation encodes its SDSS position but is not presented as a tabulated equatorial coordinate.

HVS2: Target HVS2 is also cataloged as US 708, a helium-rich subluminous sdO star (first reported by Hirsch et al. 2005). All values are from Table 1 (image I:p6-b0). Table 1 lists v_rf = 717 km/s while the text (§1.1) states the rest-frame velocity is 'at least +717 km/s'; the paper explicitly defines v_rf as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity derived from the line-of-sight velocity and not a full space velocity (T:p7-b6). Therefore it is recorded as a lower limit. The table's R_GC is the Galactocentric distance; no heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motions, or equatorial coordinates are reported for this star in the supplied material. No bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this object.

HVS3: For HVS3/HE 0437-5439, Table 1 (I:p6-b0; rendered text T:p6-b0) gives R_GC = 62 kpc, which is a Galactocentric radius, not a heliocentric distance. The table's v_rf = 548 km/s is explicitly described as a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity (T:p7-b6), so it is treated as a lower bound on the total Galactic rest-frame speed. The table's catalog entry appears as "HE 0437-54393," presumably a typographical variant of HE 0437-5439.

HVS4: Target HVS4 = SDSS J091301.01+305119.84. Table 1 (T:p6-b0; I:p6-b0) reports V=18.50 and M_V=-0.9 but no heliocentric distance; its R_GC=82 kpc is recorded as galactocentric_radius, not distance. The catalog name encodes J2000 coordinates, but no separate RA/Dec values are tabulated in the paper, so ra/dec are not extracted. The tabulated v_rf=566 km/s is explicitly the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity.

HVS5: HVS5 is SDSS J091759.48+672238.34. The paper reports no heliocentric distance, parallax, or proper motions for this star; the tabulated distance is explicitly the Galactocentric distance R_GC. Table 1 gives v_⊙ as the heliocentric radial velocity and v_rf as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity (not the full space velocity), so the latter is recorded with that condition. No bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS5.

HVS6: HVS6 is SDSS J110557.45+093439.55. Its J2000 coordinates are parsed from the SDSS identifier. Table 1 reports R_GC, not heliocentric distance, so no heliocentric distance is entered. The v_rf value of 528 km/s is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity rather than the full space velocity, so it is recorded as a lower bound. No parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS6.

HVS7: For HVS7 (SDSS J113312.12+010824.95), Table 1 lists no uncertainties. RA and Dec are not given in separate columns; they are taken directly from the SDSS catalog identifier in the table. The reported v_rf = 416 km/s is a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity and is explicitly stated not to be the full space velocity, so no total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed is reported.

HVS8: HVS8 is identified as SDSS J094214.04+200322.16 in Table 1. The RA and Dec are taken from that SDSS designation because Table 1 does not give separate equatorial-coordinate columns. Table 1 reports Galactocentric distance R_GC = 53 kpc, not a heliocentric distance. Its v_rf = 407 km/s is described as a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity from the line of sight, not the full space velocity. Table 1 does not report uncertainties for these entries, and no bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS8.

HVS9: For HVS9 (SDSS J102137.08-005234.86), Table 1 also reports v_rf = 485 km/s, but the paper defines this as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity and explicitly says it is "not a full space velocity" (T:p7-b6); therefore it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity, which requires total 3D speed, nor as radial_velocity, which is heliocentric or barycentric. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS9. The catalog identifier embeds J2000 coordinates, but no separate RA/Dec values are tabulated.

HVS10: Table 1 gives R_GC = 87 kpc as a Galactocentric radius, not a heliocentric distance. The v_rf = 432 km/s value is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity rather than a full space velocity, so it is recorded as a lower bound. Right ascension and declination are taken from the SDSS J2000 catalog designation reported for HVS10 in Table 1.

HVS11: RA and Dec are parsed from the SDSS J2000 designation SDSS J095906.48+000853.40 (T:p5-b12); the paper does not provide separate RA/Dec columns for HVS11. The reported radius is Galactocentric (R_GC), not heliocentric distance. The reported v_rf is explicitly a minimum rest-frame velocity and not a full space velocity (T:p7-b6, T:p7-b7). No parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS11.

HVS12: Target HVS12 = SDSS J105009.60+031550.67. The RA and Dec are parsed from the SDSS J2000 designation in T:p5-b14; Table 1 has no separate RA/Dec columns. The Table 1 quantity R_GC in T:p6-b0 is the Galactocentric distance, so it is recorded as galactocentric_radius rather than heliocentric distance. The Table 1 v_rf is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, not a full space velocity (T:p7-b6). No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS12.

HVS13: HVS13's R = 125 kpc is a Galactocentric radius (Table 1 column R_GC), not a heliocentric distance; no heliocentric distance is reported. The +443 km/s value is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity rather than a full space velocity, so it is recorded as a lower bound. RA and Dec are parsed from the SDSS J2000 designation; Table 1 truncates the catalog name to -000133.9 while the text gives -000133.94.

HVS14: HVS14 is SDSS J104401.75+061139.03. The paper reports its minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity as 416 km/s, but explicitly states that v_rf is not a full space velocity, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No explicit RA/Dec columns, heliocentric distance, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability are reported for HVS14. The Galactocentric distance is 112 kpc in Table 1 and approximately 110 kpc in the text.

HVS15: At T:p6-b4 the paper reports v_rf = 343 km/s as a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity. The R = 85 kpc and R = 37 kpc values are Galactocentric distances, not heliocentric distances; no heliocentric distance is explicitly reported for HVS15. No numerical bound or unbound probability is reported.

HVS16: The paper reports Galactocentric distances, not a heliocentric distance, and gives no parallax or proper motions. Table 1 defines v_rf as a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity, so it is recorded only as a lower bound on galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The 90 kpc and 44 kpc Galactocentric radii correspond, respectively, to the main-sequence and hot-BHB interpretations. RA/Dec are decoded from the SDSS J designation; Table 1 truncates the designation to ...233.8 while the text gives ...233.85. No numerical bound or unbound probability is reported.

SDSS J094014.56+530901.74: Target SDSS J094014.56+530901.74 is the first of the four "Possible HVSs" in Table 1, not one of the six newly reported unbound HVSs. The table gives R_GC = 65 kpc rather than a heliocentric distance; no parallax or proper motions are reported for this star. Table 1's v_rf column is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not full space velocity; I therefore report it as a lower bound on total Galactic rest-frame speed. The §4.2 text gives the four possible HVSs a collective main-sequence/BHB distance range of 55–85 kpc and says their minimum rest-frame velocities are around +290 km/s, while Table 1 gives 279 km/s for this target; the exact Table 1 value is retained. The identifier is printed as J094014.56+530901.7 in Table 1 and J094014.56+530901.74 in §4.2; the full §4.2 identifier is used.

SDSS J101359.79+563111.66: Target SDSS J101359.79+563111.66 (Table 1 lists it as SDSS J101359.79+563111.7) is one of the four "Possible HVSs" (type A) in Table 1 and Section 4.2. Text at T:p7-b3 additionally states the four possible HVSs have minimum rest-frame velocities around +290 km/s, main-sequence and BHB distances of 55-85 kpc, and 2-2.5 Msun masses; these are group statements, not individual values. The paper reports no individual uncertainties in Table 1 (T:p7-b7). No equatorial coordinates, parallax, heliocentric distance, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star; the only distance is the Galactocentric R_GC. The v_rf value is a line-of-sight minimum rest-frame velocity explicitly stated not to be a full space velocity (T:p7-b6); it is retained under galactic_rest_frame_velocity with that condition.

SDSS J140306.54+145005.0: Target SDSS J140306.54+145005.0 is the fourth entry of the "Possible HVSs" group in Table 1. Table 1 provides only Galactocentric distance R_GC (59 kpc), not heliocentric distance, so no `distance` value is recorded. Note a discrepancy: text (T:p7-b3) lists the four possible HVSs as SDSS J094014.56+530901.74, SDSS J101359.79+563111.66, SDSS J141342.50+442550.03, and SDSS J154556.10+243708.94, while Table 1 lists SDSS J140306.54+145005.0 instead of SDSS J141342.50+442550.03; Table A2 lists 14:13:42.51 +44:25:50.0 as a QSO, indicating the text list is likely erroneous. The target's values are taken from Table 1 as identified. No RA, Dec, parallax, proper motion, bound/unbound probability, or total space velocity is reported for this star.

SDSS J154556.10+243708.94: Target SDSS J154556.10+243708.94 (Table 1 identifier SDSS J154556.10+243708.9; also written SDSS J154556.10+243708.94 in §4.2) is one of the four "Possible HVSs" of Table 1 / §4.2. Rows in Table 1 are unlabeled for the possible HVSs and possible bound HVSs groups; the identification here is by catalog name. 

RA/Dec are not given in a table column for HVSs; they are taken from the standard SDSS J2000 designation (T:p6-b0, T:p7-b3), with the final declination digit as printed in §4.2 ("+243708.94" vs "+243708.9" in Table 1). This is the only coordinate information the paper supplies, so the sexagesimal forms are retained unconverted.

The Table 1 column v_⊙ (193 km/s) is the heliocentric radial velocity and is reported as radial_velocity. The column v_rf (293 km/s) is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, "not a full space velocity" (T:p7-b6); it is reported as a lower limit on galactic_rest_frame_velocity, not as a radial velocity, since it is referenced to the Galactic rest frame.

§4.2 additionally states that the four possible HVSs have "main-sequence star and BHB distances range 55 - 85 kpc" (T:p7-b3); because this is a group range for the four stars whose reference frame (heliocentric vs Galactocentric) is not specified, it is not entered as an individual distance value for this star. Table 1 gives only the Galactocentric distance R_GC = 83 kpc; no heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability for this star is reported.

HD 271791: The target star HD 271791 is mentioned in the paper only as a comparison example of an unbound hyper-runaway (T:p1-b6, T:p4-b4, T:p8-b7). The paper gives no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HD 271791; its only numerical association is with a former 55 M_sun binary companion, which is not a quantity for the target star. Therefore no target-star quantities are extracted.
